text:
Red squirrels have been reintroduced to the Wyrmwood reserve, according to the Wyrmwood Reintroduction Release Report, published by the Wyrmwood Reserve Trust and presented at its annual public meeting.

The report states that 48 red squirrels were released across three sites within the reserve. The first release took place on 14 April 2024.

Dr. Halvard Pemberton-Okoye, Lead Conservation Ecologist for the Wyrmwood Reserve Trust, oversaw the reintroduction. The document sets out the release locations and the number of animals placed at each stage of the programme.

The Trust presented the findings to members of the public at the meeting, where the report was made available. The reintroduction marks the return of the species to the reserve, where the Trust says it will continue its conservation work.

The Continental Record has reviewed the report's published findings. The Trust has not announced further release dates in the document.
